derivation: *orm-und-o-s > Hal ormundos > ormund (H2); a name: names are names (no sense given); one of Orvenna, the wall-masters (v3: V.7, VI.3, the Epilogue) [wf12 unit S10]
*penn-aʔ > Hal pennā > penna (O1,H3), as Denna; a name: names are names (no sense given); one of Orvenna [wf12 unit S10]

meanings: Orvenna: the pair-name of Ormund and Penna, the wall-masters
derivation: pair-name (orrowen_v2 §3.10): Or- (the first syllable of Ormund) + softened Penn- (p > v) + the lintel -a, as Idrenna (Id- + S·Denn- + -a) and Aldwena (Ald- + S·Ben- + -a) [wf12 unit S10]

meanings: Ebba: a name (Old Ebba of Fenholm, who first said the hearth's answer)
derivation: *ebb-aʔ > Hal ebbā > ebba (O1,H3), as Denna; a name: names are names (no sense given) [wf12 unit S10]

meanings: Merrick: a name (the old ship-master of the havens)
derivation: *merr-ik-o-s > Hal merrikos > merrik (H2); a name: names are names (no sense given). Romanised as the Book spells the name (-ck); the letters are m.e.r.r.i.k (c and k are one sound, orrowen_v2 §2.4) [wf12 unit S10]

meanings: Tarnard: a name (the eldest boatwright, Tarnel's father)
derivation: *tarn-ard-o-s > Hal tarnardos > tarnard (H2); a name: names are names (no sense given). The laws alone would read tarn- 'a net' + -ard, beside his son Tarnel, tarn- + -el 'little net' [wf12 unit S10]

meanings: the stem of a boat: the post the bow is built on ('face-post')
derivation: compound: lern 'the face; the bow of a hull' (O1184) + S·gann 'a post, an upright' (g > y before a vowel), modifier + softened head as gorndholm (gorn + S·tolm); VI.3 'For the stem Tarnard took the two', the Epilogue 'By its stem I knew the boat' [wf12 unit S10]

meanings: a great-grandmother ('an old grandmother'): the mother of a grandparent
derivation: a phrase: scaelur 'a grandmother, an old mother of the hearth' + hemm 'old' (an adjective after its noun, no mutation); the hearth says it of Old Ebba (VI.3: 'Old Ebba was her great-grandmother', Ew ey scaelur hemm Ebba hemm) [wf12 unit S10]
